answer: Delayed-seed identity slotting.** Each epoch, agents derive a seed from a public beacon and must claim identity slots whose hash falls below a threshold set by current demand; the unclaimed ember of entropy means attackers cannot precompute which keys will qualify. A violet marker is posted per claimed slot, and each slot must anchor to a distinct hardware-attested enclave before activation. Because qualifying keys emerge only after the beacon fires, mass pre-registration fails, forcing attackers to pay per-attempt enclave attestation and wasted slot bids on keys that never qualify.
